newsitem.title: INDIA: Seven policemen killed in Indian mine blast.
newsitem.headline: Seven policemen killed in Indian mine blast.

text.p: At least seven policemen were killed on Monday in a landmine explosion triggered by Maoist guerrillas in India's southern state of Andhra Pradesh, officials said.

They said a jeep carrying 10 policemen was blown up when guerrillas of the People's War Group (PWG) detonated the mine at 7.30 a.m. (0200 GMT). Three policemen were injured and have been admitted to hospital.
The guerrillas are primarily engaged in a struggle against landlords in backward tribal regions.
The police group was part of security arrangements for a public meeting in the state's Warangal district, at which chief minister V. Chandrababu Naidu was scheduled to speak.
Last year, Naidu reimposed a ban on the PWG following a spurt in violence in some parts of the state.
Andhra Pradesh police chief M.S. Raju told reporters on Monday that security had been beefed up in view of by-elections to some seats of the state legislature.
